topics.label: Introduction to the complement lecture
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture and outlines the general scope and challenges of learning the complement system.

topics.label: Fundamentals, nomenclature, and the central role of C3
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the foundational overview, naming conventions, and central molecular fulcrum of the complement cascade.

topics.label: Pathways of complement activation and trigger threshold
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the three pathways of complement recognition and the threshold mechanism required for activation.

topics.label: Downstream effector mechanisms of complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the primary downstream effector functions triggered by complement activation to eliminate pathogens.

topics.label: Host regulation of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes the regulatory mechanisms and host-surface proteins that prevent complement from damaging host cells.

topics.label: Clinical manifestations of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the clinical manifestations and disease phenotypes resulting from deficiencies in various complement components.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion mechanisms and applications of protein A
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic addresses the strategies used by pathogens to evade complement destruction and their practical applications in biotechnology.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and next session preview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture on complement and previews the next lecture on the adaptive immune system.
